problem: Existing navigation VLA models are reactive: fixed inference budget, no explicit reasoning, and only implicit compressed visual history as memory, causing looping and redundant exploration. Training is mostly SFT imitation, and RL work is limited to discrete autoregressive actions.
motivation: Robots in open-world settings need to deliberate when ambiguous but act fast otherwise, and to remember what was explored over long horizons. Language is better aligned with VLM pretraining than latent, visual, or map memory, and imitation alone suffers covariate shift and cannot exceed expert demonstrations.
key_idea: A single VLA (LLaVA-Video-7B + MLP continuous trajectory head) that decides per step whether to think (AdaCoT) and stores CoT-generated text summaries as persistent linguistic memory (VLingMem), trained by SFT on a 2.9M CoT dataset plus online expert-guided RL post-training.
insight: Reasoning only at ~2.1% of steps beats no CoT, per-step CoT and fixed-interval CoT; per-step dense CoT actually hurts badly (ObjNav SR 25.3 vs 50.1). Language memory alone is weak (ObjNav SR 18.8), and visual-only is decent (45.2), but combining them gives the best (50.1), so the text summaries need visual features to be usable. Online hybrid rollout (expert takeover on stuck or failed episodes) beats naive rollout, which fails to improve, and beats the DAgger-like expert rollout; RL adds about +8 SR on HM3Dv1 over SFT.
method: Dynamic FPS sampling + time-dependent grid pooling: history frames sampled at rate f_max*exp(-ΔT/s) (Ebbinghaus-style forgetting) and pooled with a stride that grows with age; SigLIP-400M features, 2-layer MLP projector, RoPE-based timestamp indicator token per frame.

AdaCoT: at each step the VLM first emits <think_on> or <think_off>; if on, it generates <think>...</think> reasoning (perception, task decomposition, visited check, next action) and a <summary>...</summary>.
VLingMem: the <summary> texts are appended to the context as persistent linguistic memory, used alongside compressed visual tokens, so history remains available even when CoT is skipped.

Action model: an MLP head on the last-token hidden state predicts a waypoint trajectory (x,y,θ); it is parameterized as a Gaussian (mean and log-std) for RL exploration, with the mean used at test time.

Nav-AdaCoT-2.9M data: HM3D ObjNav, MP3D ObjNav, OVON, EVT-Bench and HM3D Instance ImageNav trajectories; Qwen2.5-VL-72B labels CoT+summary (~472K CoT responses), filtered by rules and expert cross-check; plus 1.6M open-world video samples (LLaVA-Video-178K, ScanQA non-CoT; Video-R1 as CoT subset).
Three-stage training: (1) one epoch of video adaptive-CoT pretraining; (2) SFT co-training with loss α·MSE + (1-α)·CE, α=0.5, 20K steps, batch 512; (3) online post-training.

Online expert-guided RL: hybrid rollout mixes successful naive on-policy trajectories with shortest-path expert takeover (stuck for k=15 steps or failure); loss λ·PPO-clip (REINFORCE++ advantage) + (1-λ)·SFT loss, λ=0.01; 10 iterations of 128 episodes.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-Video-7B (Qwen2-based VLM, SigLIP-400M encoder frozen, everything else fine-tuned) + MLP action head
setting.training_data: Nav-AdaCoT-2.9M embodied navigation samples (HM3D/MP3D ObjNav, OVON, EVT-Bench, HM3D Instance ImageNav; 472K with CoT) + 1.6M open-world video samples (LLaVA-Video-178K, Video-R1, ScanQA) = 4.5M; then online RL in simulator on OVON, Instance ImageNav, and EVT-Bench DT train sets
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB video stream (no depth or pose) plus text instruction or goal image
setting.action_space: predicted continuous waypoint trajectory (x,y,θ), tracked by an NMPC controller on the real robot
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D/MP3D scenes; EVT-Bench) plus real-world Unitree Go2
setting.privileged: none at test time (a shortest-path expert is used only during RL training)

numbers.extra: single shared checkpoint across tasks; SFT + online RL

numbers_note: Real-world success rates are only given in a figure (not extractable). The ablation tables reuse the full-model numbers. The paper does not state which split HM3Dv1/v2/MP3D ObjNav or EVT-Bench/ImageNav use; 'val' and 'test' are assumed from the standard protocols.
results: VLingNav sets SOTA on HM3D ObjNav (SR 79.1/SPL 42.9 vs Uni-NaVid 73.7/37.1), HM3Dv2 (83.0 SR vs FiLM-Nav 77.0), MP3D (58.9/26.5 vs CogNav 46.6), and OVON val-unseen (SR 50.1 vs NavFoM 43.6). It also leads on EVT distracted tracking (67.6/73.5 vs TrackVLA++ 66.5/68.8) and ImageNav (60.8/37.4 vs UniGoal 60.2/23.7). One checkpoint serves all tasks and transfers zero-shot to a Unitree Go2 at ~2.5 FPS.
limitations: Monocular egocentric input with limited FOV; multi-view input is left to future work.
Single-system architecture limits action frequency and dynamic obstacle handling; the MPC waypoint controller lacks a flexible locomotion model.
SPL trails FiLM-Nav on HM3Dv2 (40.5 vs 41.3) and NavFoM on OVON val-unseen; real-world results are small-scale (10 trials per target) and reported only in a figure.
